questions.name: Rectangle Area: which rectangle needs more powder
questions.q_figure: Two upright rectangles side by side, a pink one 4 cm wide and 7 cm tall and a green one 3 cm wide and 8 cm tall, with their sides marked.
questions.s_figure: The same two rectangles with their 1 cm unit squares drawn, 28 squares in the pink one and 24 squares in the green one.

questions.name: Diagonal of a Rectangle: area of each triangle
questions.q_figure: An upright rectangle 4 cm wide and 7 cm tall with a diagonal drawn from the bottom left corner to the top right corner and the sides marked 4 cm and 7 cm.
questions.s_figure: The same rectangle with the two triangles shaded in different colours and each marked 14 cm².

questions.name: Rectangles and Squares, Q1
questions.q_figure: Figure (i): four rectangles joined in a pinwheel, with areas 28 in² at the top, 21 in² on the right, 35 in² on the left and 14 in² at the bottom, the lengths 3 in, 4 in, 7 in and 2 in marked and the width of the 14 in² rectangle shown as ? in; figure (ii): a rectangle 4 m tall made of a dotted 29 m² piece with a blank piece below it, an 11 m² hatched piece beside the top, the dotted piece and the blank piece together outlined and marked 50 m², and ? on the missing sides.
questions.s_figure: Figure (i) with the unknown sides found as 3 in, 4 in, 5 in and 2 in, and figure (ii) with the top widths 7.25 m and 2.75 m and the lower height of about 2.9 m marked.

questions.q_figure: A large rectangle ABCD with a smaller green rectangle EFGH inside it and the region between them shaded as a path, followed by three more copies of ABCD in which EFGH sits in different positions inside it.
questions.s_figure: ABCD marked 20 m by 14 m and EFGH marked 16 m by 10 m, with the path split into two long strips and two short strips each 2 m wide.

questions.q_figure: A rectangular plot with sides 14 m and 12 m crossed by one vertical path and one horizontal path, each drawn as a pair of parallel lines, so that the two paths cross in the plot.
questions.s_figure: The same plot with the width of the 14 m path marked p, the width of the 12 m path marked q and the p by q square where the paths cross marked.

questions.q_figure: A spiral tube of the same width 1 drawn as a red outline, with its straight parts marked 20 along the top, 20 down the right side, 20 along the bottom, 15 up the left side, 15 across, 10 down, 10 back, 5 up and 5 across, and the width 1 marked at both ends.
questions.s_figure: An L shaped bend with arms 5 and 5 drawn beside a straight tube of width 1 and unknown length, with the corner square shared by the two arms marked.

questions.q_figure: A square with its diagonal drawn from the bottom left corner to the top right corner and a line from the top left corner to the middle of that diagonal, the two halves of the diagonal marked equal, so that the square is cut into regions 1, 2 and 3.
questions.s_figure: The square and a square of double the side drawn side by side, each cut into regions 1, 2 and 3 in the same way.

questions.q_figure: A square with two perpendicular lines drawn inside it, not parallel to the sides, one running from the top side to the bottom side and the other from the left side to the right side, with a right angle marked where they cross.
questions.s_figure: The four pieces of the square rearranged into a larger square with a square hole in the middle.

questions.name: Triangle Area: area of triangle XDC
questions.q_figure: A rectangle ABCD with A and B on the top and D and C on the bottom, DC = 5 cm along the bottom and the height 4 cm on the left, a point X on the top side AB joined to D and to C, and the perpendicular XY from X down to DC with a right angle at Y.
questions.s_figure: The same rectangle split by XY into two rectangles, each cut in half by XD or XC, with the triangle XDC shaded as half of the whole rectangle.

questions.name: Triangles, Q1
questions.q_figure: Three triangles: ABC with a dotted height AE of 3 cm to the base BC marked 4 cm; DEF with the side EF marked 5 cm and a dotted perpendicular DN of 3.2 cm from D to EF; and a right triangle NAT with the right angle at A, NA 4 cm and AT 3 cm.
An isosceles triangle SUB with S at the top and U and B on the base, the equal sides SU and SB marked with ticks, and SE drawn from S perpendicular to UB with a right angle at E.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with the triangles SEB and SUE both marked 24 sq. units.

questions.name: Using the Area Formula: finding the height BY
questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with BC = 5 along the bottom, a perpendicular AX of length 3 from A to X on BC, the side AC = 4, and a perpendicular BY from B to the side AC meeting it at Y.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with its area written two ways, 1/2 × 5 × 3 on the base BC and 1/2 × 4 × BY on the base AC, and BY marked 3.75.

questions.name: Triangles, Q2
questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with BC = 6 units on the bottom line, AC = 8 units, the vertical height AX = 4 units from A down to a point X on the line CB just left of B, and the line BY from B perpendicular to AC meeting it at Y.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with its area written two ways, 1/2 × 6 × 4 on the base BC and 1/2 × 8 × BY on the base AC, and BY marked 3 units.

questions.q_figure: Three identical squares ABCD, BCEF and BFGH, with ABCD on the left, BCEF to its right and BFGH above BCEF so that H is directly above B, the triangle DCH shaded red and the part of square ABCD to the left of the line DH shaded blue.
questions.s_figure: The line DH crossing AB at its midpoint, with the red triangle DCH and the small blue triangle at the left of ABCD marked with their sides in terms of the side s of a square.

questions.q_figure: A triangle XYZ with M the midpoint of XY and N the midpoint of XZ marked with ticks and the line MN drawn.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with NY drawn, showing the triangle XMN as half of XNY and XNY as half of XYZ.

questions.q_figure: A map with two parallel lines for a river, a dot for the water tank just below the river and a dot for the house lower down and to the left.
questions.s_figure: The tank reflected across the river bank, with a straight line from the house to the reflection crossing the bank at the best landing point.

questions.name: Area of any Polygon, Q1
questions.q_figure: A long thin quadrilateral ABCD with the diagonal AC = 22 cm, B above and D below it, and BM and DN drawn perpendicular to AC with BM = 3 cm and DN = 3 cm, M near C and N near A.
questions.s_figure: The same quadrilateral split by AC into the triangles ABC and ACD, each marked with base 22 cm, height 3 cm and area 33 cm².

questions.q_figure: A rectangle ABCD with AB = 18 cm along the top and BC = 10 cm, E on AB with AE = 10 cm and EB = 8 cm, F on AD with AF = 6 cm and FD = 4 cm, and the region FECD shaded.
questions.s_figure: The same rectangle with the two unshaded triangles AEF and EBC marked, to be taken away from the whole rectangle.

questions.q_figure: A rectangle with a point inside it near the right side, one blue triangle standing on the top side with its tip at that point and another blue triangle standing on the bottom side with its tip at the same point.
questions.s_figure: The same rectangle with a line through the point parallel to the top and bottom sides, showing the two heights of the blue triangles adding up to the full height of the rectangle.

questions.name: Parallelograms, Q1
questions.q_figure: Seven parallelograms (a) to (g) drawn on a grid, all with the same base and the same height between two grid lines, leaning by different amounts, some to the left and some to the right.

Four parallelograms: (i) base 7 cm with a dotted height of 4 cm; (ii) base 5 cm with a dotted height of 3 cm and a diagonal drawn; (iii) a slanting side of 5 cm with a dotted perpendicular of 4.8 cm drawn to it; (iv) a slanting side of 2 cm with a dotted perpendicular of 4.4 cm drawn to it.
A parallelogram PQRS with SR = 12 cm along the bottom, QM = 6 cm drawn from Q perpendicular to SR at M, PS = 7.6 cm on the left side, and QN drawn from Q perpendicular to the line PS meeting it at N.
questions.s_figure: The same parallelogram with its area written two ways, 12 × 6 on the base SR and 7.6 × QN on the base PS.

questions.q_figure: A 5 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a parallelogram drawn on the same 5 cm base, its slanting sides 4 cm, leaning to the right and overlapping the rectangle.
An isosceles triangle ABC with the altitude AD drawn from A to the base BC and a right angle marked at D.
questions.s_figure: The two right triangles ADB and ADC cut apart and joined along their slanting sides to make a rectangle.

questions.name: Trapezium Area: ABCD and WXYZ on a grid
questions.q_figure: Two trapeziums on a grid: ABCD with a right angle at D, AB = 4 squares, DC = 6 squares and the vertical side AD = 4 squares, and WXYZ with WX = 5 squares, ZY = 9 squares, height 4 squares and the points M and N on ZY each 2 squares in from the ends Z and Y.
questions.s_figure: Each trapezium split by dotted heights into a rectangle or square and one or two right triangles, with the areas 16 and 4 written on the pieces of ABCD and 4, 20 and 4 on the pieces of WXYZ.

questions.name: Rhombus and Trapezium, Q3
questions.q_figure: Four trapeziums: (i) a tilted one with parallel sides 10 ft and 7 ft and 16 ft marked between them; (ii) parallel sides 24 m on top and 36 m at the bottom with a dotted height of 14 m; (iii) parallel sides 14 in on the left and 6 in on the right with 10 in marked between them; (iv) parallel sides 12 ft on top and 18 ft at the bottom with a dotted height of 8 ft.

A trapezium ABCD with the shorter side AB on top and the longer side DC at the bottom, I and J the midpoints of the slanting sides AD and BC, and a dotted rectangle EFGH with H and E on the line AB and G and F on DC, its vertical sides passing through I and J.
questions.s_figure: The trapezium with the congruent pairs of corner triangles AHI and DGI, and BEJ and CFJ, marked, which fill the rectangle EFGH.

questions.q_figure: A regular hexagon with one long diagonal drawn from its lower left vertex to its upper right vertex and a vertical line from the middle of that diagonal down to the bottom vertex, dividing it into a trapezium on top, an equilateral triangle at the lower left and a rhombus at the lower right.
A trapezium ZYXW with ZY parallel to WX and ZY the shorter top side, A the midpoint of the slanting side XY marked with ticks, and the line ZA extended beyond A to meet the line WX extended at B.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the triangles ZYA and BXA marked congruent.
